target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe AMD's strategy of leveraging core IP to develop semi-custom solutions through co-development with console and handheld PC manufacturers. D039 details the collaborative approach and tailored products (SoCs/APUs), while D033 explicitly lists the specific clients (PS5, Xbox, Steam Deck) benefiting from these tailored solutions.

Both disclosures identify the same specific semi-custom products powering the Sony PlayStation 5, Microsoft Xbox Series S/X, and Valve Steam Deck. The 2024 disclosure adds the PS5 Pro but retains the core subject of the specific gaming hardware partners.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom operate in the custom silicon space, but AMD focuses on tailored semi-custom SoCs for gaming consoles and handhelds, whereas Broadcom provides IP and platforms for customers to design their own ASICs for AI, HPC, and networking. AMD’s approach is described as 'customer-specific solutions' powered by its own CPU/GPU tech for specific hardware partners (Sony, Microsoft, Valve), while Broadcom’s model enables external customers to build 'application specific integrated circuits' using Broadcom's underlying technology platforms.

sentences.text: Our semi-custom products are tailored, high-performance, customer-specific solutions based on CPU, GPU and multi-media technologies.
AMD semi-custom SoC products power the Sony PlayStation® 5, the Microsoft ® Xbox Series S™ and X™ game consoles, as well as the Valve Steam Deck PC.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Intel Arc graphics family powers immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, Intel launched the Arc B-Series based on Xe2 architecture, featuring second-generation Xe-cores that deliver 70% more performance per core and 50% better power efficiency than the Intel Arc A750.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose capabilities in discrete graphics for gaming. AMD leverages its GPU technology in its semi-custom console products (e.g., PS5, Xbox) and PC gaming, while Intel markets its Arc graphics family for 'immersive games' and discrete client GPUs. However, AMD’s primary gaming hardware narrative is tied to its custom console SoC partnerships, whereas Intel’s disclosure focuses on its standalone discrete GPU product line for PCs rather than custom console silicon.

The Intel® Arc™ graphics family offers modern GPU features to power immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, we launched the Intel Arc B-Series based on the latest Xe2 GPU architecture. The compute engine of the Intel Arc B-Series is our second-generation Xe-core, which delivers 70% more performance per core and is 50% more power efficient than the Intel Arc A750.

comparisons.peer_summary: GDDR is a high-performance memory solution optimized for high-bandwidth workloads in graphics cards, gaming consoles, and high-performance computing applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron identify gaming consoles as a key application market for their respective semiconductor products. AMD designs the central processing and graphics silicon (SoCs) that power these consoles, while Micron designs and manufactures the Graphics DRAM (GDDR) memory that is optimized for the high-bandwidth workloads required by these devices. Both companies treat 'gaming consoles' as a specific, defined end-market for their core technologies.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming products include GeForce RTX and GTX GPUs for desktop/laptop PCs, GeForce NOW cloud gaming, and SoCs/development services for game consoles.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA explicitly disclose providing System-on-Chips (SoCs) and development services for game consoles as part of their gaming product portfolios. AMD states its semi-custom products power the PS5, Xbox, and Steam Deck, while NVIDIA lists 'SoCs and development services for game consoles' alongside its GeForce PC GPUs and GeForce NOW cloud gaming services, indicating a shared business segment involving custom hardware provision for the console market.

peer_results.rationale: The supplied candidates for QCOM focus on mobile SoCs for smartphones, consumer IoT, and AI PCs. While Qualcomm also uses SoC architecture, its disclosed gaming-related activities are limited to mobile/gaming on handheld devices, lacking the specific 'gaming console' or 'semi-custom console SoC' business segment that defines the comparable AMD disclosure.
